match.userMessage: Again, no bullet points or numbered lists with me, please. Plain sentences only.

response.content: Understood, T — sorry about that, my last reply still came across as a list even though I wrote in sentences. Let me try again properly blended together: Sintra is the easiest and most classic option, just forty minutes from Rossio station, with its hilltop palaces and cool forested hills offering a nice break from Lisbon's heat, though it's best visited early before the tour buses arrive. If you'd rather escape the crowds, Óbidos is about an hour away and gives you a walled medieval town with narrow cobbled streets, castle ramparts you can walk along, and the local cherry liqueur ginjinha served in little chocolate cups, all of which can be comfortably explored in an afternoon. And if you're after something coastal, Setúbal is roughly an hour from Lisbon and combines access to the cliffs and beaches of the Arrábida natural park with some of the best fried cuttlefish you'll find anywhere in Portugal, making it a good change of pace from the more inland, historic feel of the other two. Let me know if you'd like help working out train times for any of them.
